options: The same named metric producing different values over time or in different places, without a business reason
A dashboard loading slowly
A metric being deleted on purpose
A user losing their password
questions.explain: Drift is when a named number stops meaning the same thing everywhere, so values diverge for reasons unrelated to the business.

questions.q: Which is an example of a source change that can cause drift even when metric logic is unchanged?
options: A dashboard title is capitalized
The metric owner takes a vacation
A picklist value such as an opportunity stage is renamed or a new stage is added
A user changes their profile photo
questions.explain: Metric filters depend on real values in Salesforce. If those values change, the metric's inputs change without any edit to its logic.

questions.q: Someone needs a version of a metric that includes open pipeline. What prevents drift?
options: Edit the original metric so everyone gets the new logic
Create a separate, clearly named metric for the different meaning
Copy the calculation into a personal dashboard
Rename the original to something vague
questions.explain: Different meanings deserve different named metrics, so the original definition remains stable.

questions.q: What is the purpose of running a SOQL check such as summing Amount where IsWon is true for the current fiscal quarter?
options: To permanently change the metric's definition
To speed up the dashboard
To delete Opportunity records
To reconcile the metric against an independently computed source and reveal drift
questions.explain: An independent calculation over the same period and filters should match the metric. A mismatch signals drift, or sync timing that you should account for.

questions.q: Why should you note data refresh times when reconciling a metric against SOQL?
options: SOQL cannot query Opportunities
The semantic model may read synced data, so differences can come from sync timing rather than definition drift
Refresh times determine the Salesforce license price
Reconciliation is only valid at midnight
questions.explain: SOQL reads the source system live, while the model may read data synced through Data 360, so timing can explain gaps.
